# Phase 1: the techniques and the planner

Part of the [`ci-doctor`](../../SKILL.md) hub. What [Phase 1](../phases/phase-1-map-the-repo.md) needs from the guide and the reference READMEs, copied from them so the phase runs where only the skills are installed. Each part links its source.

## The techniques

Every technique in guide sections 2–17, by section, each with when it applies and when to skip it. Mark each that applies and bears on the measured limiter, and read its section only then.

- **[2. Runners, Blacksmith, and the cost of getting fast](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md)**
  - [Choosing a provider and runners](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#choosing-a-provider-and-runners): **Applies when:** The plan picks a provider, or sizes or resizes runners, on any CI platform. **Skip when:** The baseline shows neither runner cost nor runner size affecting the bottleneck.
  - [When jobs wait to start](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#when-jobs-wait-to-start): **Applies when:** The slowest tenth of jobs wait minutes for a runner, or queue time makes up a large share of PR wait time. **Skip when:** Queue time is only seconds, as on most repos.
  - [Why we recommend Blacksmith](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#why-we-recommend-blacksmith): **Applies when:** The repo runs GitHub Actions on GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runners, and the baseline shows where queue, compute, or setup time goes. **Skip when:** The repo is off GitHub Actions, or the user declines the move (the plan stays on the current runners).
  - [Setting up Blacksmith](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#setting-up-blacksmith): **Applies when:** The user approved a move to Blacksmith. **Skip when:** The plan stays on the current runners.
  - [Getting fast costs money and time first](../../../../docs/pages/02-runners-blacksmith-and-the-cost-of-getting-fast.md#getting-fast-costs-money-and-time-first): **Applies when:** The plan prices its own optimization period: sweeps, replays, measurement runs, bisects, and debugging. **Skip when:** The plan changes nothing that runs in CI.
- **[3. Workflow anatomy](../../../../docs/pages/03-workflow-anatomy.md)**: **Applies when:** The repo is on GitHub Actions and its workflow lacks a plan job that gates the others, or a single result job that verifies them. **Skip when:** The workflow already gates every job on a plan and checks them in one result job.
- **[4. Run only what a change can reach](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md)**
  - [Drafts and concurrency](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#drafts-and-concurrency): **Applies when:** PR workflows run on drafts, or a draft event or old rerun can cancel the newest head's run. **Skip when:** Every job already skips drafts and concurrency groups keep ready PRs, drafts, reruns, manual runs, and merges isolated.
  - [A selector built from a real dependency graph](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#a-selector-built-from-a-real-dependency-graph): **Applies when:** A pnpm workspace's TypeScript tests (`.test.ts` or `.test.tsx`) run in full on every PR. **Skip when:** Tests are in other languages or named differently (keep their jobs running in full until a selector maps them), or the repo uses Turborepo or Nx (start with its built-in affected run first).
  - [Turborepo and Nx: their own affected runs first](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#turborepo-and-nx-their-own-affected-runs-first): **Applies when:** The repo uses Turborepo or Nx and does no selection today. **Skip when:** The repo uses neither.
  - ["Near" selection for an integration-heavy server](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#near-selection-for-an-integration-heavy-server): **Applies when:** Every integration test boots the whole server, making the import graph say everything reaches everything, and `main`'s sweeps run the full suite as a safety net. **Skip when:** The import graph already narrows selection, or no sweep on `main` covers what "near" leaves out.
  - [CI file changes run only the jobs they touch](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#ci-file-changes-run-only-the-jobs-they-touch): **Applies when:** A selector exists and editing a workflow or composite action still triggers every job. **Skip when:** No selector exists yet, or CI edits already run only affected jobs.
  - [Other narrowing](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#other-narrowing): **Applies when:** Real-container tests, packaging, or a Rust service run on every PR regardless of what changed. **Skip when:** None of those run unconditionally on PRs.
  - [Verify the selector like production code](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#verify-the-selector-like-production-code): **Applies when:** A selector, or any change to one, is proposed. **Skip when:** Selection isn't changing.
- **[5. Tiers: what runs where](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md)**: **Applies when:** Checks too slow or costly for every PR could move to merges, `main`'s server runs, or a sweep instead. **Skip when:** No sweep has yet proven it runs every check you want to take off PRs (see [Releasing what the sweep checked](#releasing-what-the-sweep-checked) below).
  - [Moving heavy tests to the right tier](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#moving-heavy-tests-to-the-right-tier): **Applies when:** Expensive files run on every PR: bounded model checks, large-fixture or long-history/large-dataset tests, wide grids, or full oracle corpora. **Skip when:** No PR test is expensive enough to tie to the specific inputs it proves.
  - [Cron is not a scheduler you can trust](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#cron-is-not-a-scheduler-you-can-trust): **Applies when:** GitHub's scheduled runs carry checks such as sweeps or `main`-only jobs. **Skip when:** The repo has no scheduled or `main`-only jobs.
  - [One issue for a red main, and a bisect with a budget](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#one-issue-for-a-red-main-and-a-bisect-with-a-budget): **Applies when:** A sweep on `main` runs checks that PRs skip, so failures must be traced back to a merge. **Skip when:** `main` has no sweep.
  - [Releasing what the sweep checked](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md#releasing-what-the-sweep-checked): **Applies when:** Any PR coverage is moving to a sweep, or releases and deploys should ship only what the sweep checked. **Skip when:** PRs keep all their coverage.
- **[6. Reuse work by its real inputs](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md)**
  - [Task runners and their remote caches](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#task-runners-and-their-remote-caches): **Applies when:** The repo already uses a workspace task runner or caches task results. **Skip when:** You would adopt a runner solely for its cache and haven't done section 4's selection replay yet.
  - [Checking a cache on another task runner](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#checking-a-cache-on-another-task-runner): **Applies when:** Replays come from a runner with declared inputs (Turborepo, Nx, Bazel, or Gradle). **Skip when:** The runner tracks actual file reads (like Vite+), or nothing is cached.
  - [A remote task cache, with tests as tasks](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#a-remote-task-cache-with-tests-as-tasks): **Applies when:** Task results are shared through a remote cache (on Vite+ as written, or on other runners via the table above). **Skip when:** No task results are shared across machines.
  - [Setting up the remote task cache on Cloudflare, step by step](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#setting-up-the-remote-task-cache-on-cloudflare-step-by-step): **Applies when:** The plan self-hosts Vite+'s remote cache on Cloudflare and the trust policy is already decided. **Skip when:** Using another runner's cache, a hosted cache, or the trust policy is still undecided.
  - [Rust: reuse passes and binaries separately](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#rust-reuse-passes-and-binaries-separately): **Applies when:** The stack includes Rust. **Skip when:** There is no Rust code.
  - [Setup caches on Blacksmith](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#setup-caches-on-blacksmith): **Applies when:** Dependency installs and toolchain setup take significant job time (via Blacksmith sticky disks, or the Actions cache fallback elsewhere). **Skip when:** Setup is not a meaningful share of job time.
  - [Not worth caching](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#not-worth-caching): **Applies when:** Someone proposes caching sub-second generation, npm tarballs, Rust `sccache` in CI, or another cache layer. **Skip when:** No new cache layer is being proposed.
- **[7. Shards, runners and billing](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md)**
  - [Shards from measured time, not file count](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#shards-from-measured-time-not-file-count): **Applies when:** Tests run (or should run) across multiple shards and per-file timings on `main` are recorded. **Skip when:** Per-file timings aren't recorded yet.
  - [Work stealing over cache-key claims](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#work-stealing-over-cache-key-claims): **Applies when:** Time-based fixed shards are already in place and runner speed still varies—measured on its own. **Skip when:** Fixed time-based shards aren't in place yet.
  - [Independent lanes](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#independent-lanes): **Applies when:** A shard runs workers in synchronized rounds, forcing faster lanes to wait for the slowest task in each round. **Skip when:** Each worker lane already starts its next task immediately upon finishing.
  - [Size runners from the work and the bill](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#size-runners-from-the-work-and-the-bill): **Applies when:** Per-job CPU over at least three runs (including the high tail) shows a runner is mis-sized, or tiny selections are paying a large runner's minimum-minute cost. **Skip when:** Fewer than three runs agree.
  - [Shorten the critical path before buying cores](../../../../docs/pages/07-shards-runners-and-billing.md#shorten-the-critical-path-before-buying-cores): **Applies when:** Jobs sit idle waiting on upstream jobs before starting setup, or compiled test binaries run sequentially. **Skip when:** The critical path is already bounded by a single job's own work.
- **[8. A cheaper test harness](../../../../docs/pages/08-a-cheaper-test-harness.md)**: **Applies when:** Tests boot a heavy server runtime per file (such as `workerd` under Vitest). **Skip when:** Runtime startup and bundling make up only a small share of each test file's time.
- **[9. Workspace tooling](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md)**
  - [The commands](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#the-commands): **Applies when:** A TypeScript workspace adopting commands one at a time where a duplicate pass or measured bottleneck justifies it. **Skip when:** Existing commands show neither—keep them as they are.
  - [One type check, no duplicate passes](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#one-type-check-no-duplicate-passes): **Applies when:** Framework diagnostics or type-aware lint run as a separate compiler pass. **Skip when:** A single type pass already covers them.
  - [Every file in a project, enforced](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#every-file-in-a-project-enforced): **Applies when:** One consolidated type check covers the workspace via project references. **Skip when:** Each project is checked independently.
  - [Type results follow content across worktrees](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#type-results-follow-content-across-worktrees): **Applies when:** Several worktrees type-check the same projects on one machine. **Skip when:** Each machine has only one checkout.
  - [Type-aware lint where it pays](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#type-aware-lint-where-it-pays): **Applies when:** The linter has type-aware rules and local checks run them across the whole repo while multiple agents check concurrently. **Skip when:** The linter has no type-aware rules.
  - [Keep lint config out of the test config](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#keep-lint-config-out-of-the-test-config): **Applies when:** Lint settings live in the config tests load, causing lint edits to invalidate test transforms and cached test keys. **Skip when:** Tests already load a separate config.
  - [Custom lint rules that guard the shortcuts](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#custom-lint-rules-that-guard-the-shortcuts): **Applies when:** The repo takes shortcuts a lint rule can guard: explicit build inputs, seeded property tests, restricted runtimes, or package boundaries. **Skip when:** None of those apply.
  - [No build before checking or testing](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#no-build-before-checking-or-testing): **Applies when:** Workspace packages must be built before type checks or tests can import them. **Skip when:** Workspace packages already resolve directly to source.
  - [Generated files](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#generated-files): **Applies when:** Checks, tests, or builds depend on generated files. **Skip when:** Nothing is generated.
  - [Find existing code before writing more](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#find-existing-code-before-writing-more): **Applies when:** Agents write code in the repo (note: this is a warm local benefit, not a measured CI saving). **Skip when:** No agents write code here.
  - [Pin everything, share the tool](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#pin-everything-share-the-tool): **Applies when:** Node, pnpm, or shared tool versions float, or the static workflow stops at its first failure. **Skip when:** Versions are pinned and every static command reports its results.
  - [If you use Effect](../../../../docs/pages/09-workspace-tooling.md#if-you-use-effect): **Applies when:** The stack uses Effect. **Skip when:** It doesn't.
- **[10. Slow tests: the method](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md)**
  - [Find them from CI's own records, not intuition](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#find-them-from-cis-own-records-not-intuition): **Applies when:** Test time contributes to the measured bottleneck and CI records per-file durations. **Skip when:** Per-file records don't exist yet—add recording first (section 13).
  - [Name the wait before changing anything](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#name-the-wait-before-changing-anything): **Applies when:** A file past 10 s—or a shard-ending file—is on the inventory. **Skip when:** The inventory is empty.
  - [Keep what each test proves](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#keep-what-each-test-proves): **Applies when:** Any test is modified to run faster. **Skip when:** No tests change.
  - [Measure honestly](../../../../docs/pages/10-slow-tests-the-method.md#measure-honestly): **Applies when:** Reporting a before/after speedup or any timing comparison. **Skip when:** Nothing is being compared.
- **[11. Flakes](../../../../docs/pages/11-flakes.md)**: **Applies when:** CI records show tests that failed and then passed, or jobs that passed on rerun. **Skip when:** Records show no failed-then-passed tests or jobs.
- **[12. Budgets, health and spend](../../../../docs/pages/12-budgets-health-and-spend.md)**: **Applies when:** The plan sets job or run budgets, a spend cap, or a health report, or a baseline compares spend across windows. **Skip when:** None of those is proposed or measured.
- **[13. Records: evidence of what ran](../../../../docs/pages/13-records-evidence-of-what-ran.md)**: **Applies when:** CI cannot prove which test files actually executed, or per-file timings are missing. **Skip when:** The repo already logs every executed file and its duration on each run.
  - [Collecting from the API without losing runs](../../../../docs/pages/13-records-evidence-of-what-ran.md#collecting-from-the-api-without-losing-runs): **Applies when:** Building a baseline, audit, or report from the CI provider's API. **Skip when:** All evidence comes from the repo's own records.
- **[14. Local speed, and many agents on one machine](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md)**
  - [Fast local feedback](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md#fast-local-feedback): **Applies when:** Agents or engineers wait on local checks. **Skip when:** Local checks already run only what covers the change.
  - [The local runner contract](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md#the-local-runner-contract): **Applies when:** A local runner executes a selected subset of tests (such as `test:cached` or a custom driver). **Skip when:** Local runs don't use selection.
  - [Sharing one machine](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md#sharing-one-machine): **Applies when:** Multiple agents or worktrees run tests concurrently on one shared host. **Skip when:** Each machine runs a single checkout.
- **[15. The agent workflow around CI](../../../../docs/pages/15-the-agent-workflow-around-ci.md)**: **Applies when:** Agents open, mark ready, and merge the repo's PRs. **Skip when:** Humans run the PR workflow—keep the repo's existing trigger and merge policy until the user approves a change.
  - [How we run a review](../../../../docs/pages/15-the-agent-workflow-around-ci.md#how-we-run-a-review): **Applies when:** A repo adopts the review gate without an existing review process for what the gate requires. **Skip when:** The repo already defines who reviews and how, or doesn't gate CI on a review.
  - [Running a slow-test campaign with parallel agents](../../../../docs/pages/15-the-agent-workflow-around-ci.md#running-a-slow-test-campaign-with-parallel-agents): **Applies when:** The slow-file inventory is large enough to divide across agents, and your harness can run parallel agents in separate worktrees. **Skip when:** Your harness doesn't support parallel agents, or one agent can handle the list.
- **[16. Standing automations](../../../../docs/pages/16-standing-automations.md)**: **Applies when:** A recurring read-only or deterministic follow-up would otherwise be run by hand, and the user approves its schedule. **Skip when:** The user hasn't approved a schedule—a manual, read-only follow-up is the default.
- **[17. Keeping agent knowledge from going stale](../../../../docs/pages/17-keeping-agent-knowledge-from-going-stale.md)**
  - [Where knowledge lives](../../../../docs/pages/17-keeping-agent-knowledge-from-going-stale.md#where-knowledge-lives): **Applies when:** Agents work in the repo and the plan's findings need to live in their instructions. **Skip when:** No agents work in the repo.
  - [What keeps it fresh](../../../../docs/pages/17-keeping-agent-knowledge-from-going-stale.md#what-keeps-it-fresh): **Applies when:** The repo maintains lessons or a tried-and-dropped register that agents read. **Skip when:** No agents work in the repo.

## 18. Tried and dropped

From [docs/pages/18-tried-and-dropped.md](../../../../docs/pages/18-tried-and-dropped.md). What was tried and dropped, and what would have to change before trying again.

**When** marks the week of our six-week effort in which we tested or decided an idea. **Outcome** records what ruled it out: *measured*, *modelled*, or *replayed* and rejected; *shipped then replaced* or *removed*; *folded into another change*; or *rejected on principle*. The final column notes what replaced it or what must change before retrying. In this public copy, our internal PR and run links are omitted; your own register should include an `Evidence` column matching the template in [`ci-read-what-was-tried`](../checks/ci-read-what-was-tried.md).

| When | Idea | Outcome | What we saw | Lesson | Replaced by, or retry when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | Local-only pre-merge checks, no CI | Shipped then replaced | Runner spend dropped to zero during the interval, with no controlled total-cost or reliability comparison recorded | Zero CI bill isn't a measured saving | Dedicated-runner CI |
| Weeks 1–2 | Many tiny parallel jobs (39) | Measured and rejected | Faster completion, but substantially more rounded runner minutes than packed jobs | Include setup and billing rounding in the model | Fewer, fuller jobs; retry only if setup and rounding stop dominating |
| Week 2 | Arm runners for JS tests | Measured and rejected | Tests ran ~30% slower and three integration files failed, despite ~37% cheaper per-minute pricing | Unit price isn't service price | Keep Arm for native builds; retry when the same tests match speed and pass |
| Week 2 | Specialized checkout cache (mirrored checkout) | Rejected | Standard checkout was already cheap, while the mirror billed persistent storage | Measure fixed work before adding persistent storage | Repos with multi-GB checkouts |
| Week 2 | Docker layer caching for clean, verified builds | Rejected | Conflicted with our clean-build contract; verified images were already reused by content tag | Reuse only independently verified complete images | — |
| Weeks 2 and 4 | Dependency disk holding only `node_modules` | Measured and rejected | Installs and postinstalls still ran because their markers lived in the store outside the disk | Preserve and verify the complete install: toolchain, store markers, and workspace links | Complete-install disk ([section 6](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#setup-caches-on-blacksmith)) |
| Week 2 | Vitest isolation, pools, and module caches | Measured and rejected | Shards spent nearly all their time inside the tests themselves | Bottlenecks were single slow files and waits, not runner overhead | Retry when import or transform time is a real share of shard time |
| Week 2 | One job per test file (or per part of a file) | Measured and rejected | Each slice used roughly one core in four | Per-job setup and minute rounding dominate | Never, while setup is billed per job |
| Week 2 | Vitest `--changed` / import-graph selection over a whole-Worker harness | Replayed and rejected | Selected 494 of 1,035 files for one edit; median 19% fewer files but ~0 billed minutes saved; missed 13 disk readers; slow to compute | Static imports don't capture integration coverage | Near selection plus sweeps, then explicit coverage edges (section 4) |
| Week 2 | Automatic input tracking for every build | Measured and rejected (for builds) | Hit `spawn EBUSY` on our dev platform; subprocess reads raised correctness concerns too | Use explicit build inputs guarded by a completeness lint rule | Retry when tracking works on every dev platform; tests use it today (section 6) |
| Week 2 | Time-balanced shards before splitting giant files | Modelled and deferred | Can't balance shards while one file exceeds a shard's share | Split giant files first, then balance | Shipped after splitting long files (section 7) |
| Week 2 | 9 workers on 8 vCPU | Measured and rejected | Took 1.5–1.8× as long as 6 workers, with timing failures | Spare CPU isn't spare capacity | — |
| Week 2 | Ordinary tests after every merge | Folded into another change | Closed proposal, superseded before measurement | Batch broad checks; keep per-merge type checks | Sweeps (section 5) |
| Week 3 | Halving a timer-heavy job's runner | Measured and rejected | Each file ran 30–45% slower with saturated CPU for only a small saving | Keep burst headroom | — |
| Week 3 | Shared-machine Docker admission | Shipped then removed | Dedicated CI replaced the shared box; removing the forwarding socket hung most runs, so it stayed | A removal can depend on an undocumented dependency | — |
| Week 3 | Human-picked extra slow/sandbox coverage on PRs | Shipped then removed | Extra catches were all flakes; zero real failures across 81 slow jobs | Broad pre-merge coverage must prove observed value | Changed files on PRs, rest in sweeps |
| Week 4 | Rebuilding macOS release binaries less often | Modelled and rejected | Every macOS job was a real release; binaries embed their version and the service pairs only with its own release | Unchanged source doesn't make an old binary valid for a new release | Fewer releases, or an intentional version-contract redesign |
| Week 4 | 10× faster test clock to get a shard file under 90 s | Measured and rejected | One case lacked enough real time for its work and flaked in CI | Shorten a deadline only when remaining real time still covers work on a busy runner | Real-clock deadlines sized to actual work |
| Week 4 | Long-lived binaries and tarballs as artifacts | Shipped then replaced | Exhausted artifact storage and broke sweeps | Match retention to usefulness | Cache handoffs and short retention (a later outage exposed what still relied on artifacts, section 19) |
| Week 4 | Staging-connected recording/proof extension | Shipped then reverted | Landed, reverted, and remaining hooks removed | A closed or reverted experiment alone doesn't establish why it was rejected | Deterministic recording/replay stayed; revert reason wasn't recorded |
| Week 4 | Reusing imported state across server files | Measured and rejected | State leaks failed 8 tests across 6 files on a second run | A single green run doesn't prove isolation | — |
| Week 4 | Lower Go memory limits for the type checker | Measured and rejected | 50–80% slower to save <2 GB | Live heap sets the floor | Go backend only; since replaced by `tsrs` (section 9) |
| Week 4 | Trimming what TypeScript loads to speed up checking | Measured, kept, no speed-up | Fewer declarations loaded, but checking time didn't move | Scheduling, not loading, set wall time | Retry when the checker becomes load-bound |
| Week 4 | Splitting test files further to shorten shards | Rejected | Every extra file pays another harness start | Split only files past the per-file limit | — |
| Weeks 4–5 | Whole-tree hash test-pass cache | Shipped then replaced | Replayed 0 of 4,872 file runs across 7 sweeps | Key by what each task actually reads | Tracked-read tasks (section 6) |
| Weeks 4–6 | Rust in CI: `lld`/`mold`, 256 codegen units, opt-level tweaks, one combined test binary, `sccache`, shared compile with packaging | Measured and rejected | Negligible, slower, or lost fidelity; combined binary broke 3 tests | Profile before tuning the compiler | — |
| Undated | Shared Cargo `target/` dir across worktrees | Rejected | Returned another worktree's binary as "fresh" | mtime freshness isn't content identity | Per-worktree `target/` + `sccache` |
| Weeks 4–6 | Shared runtime / watch mode across test files | Measured and rejected | Saved <10% per file and broke isolation (module state, alarms, DB names) | Share compilation, not runtime state | — |
| Weeks 4–6 | Resident incremental bundler | Measured and rejected | Roughly halved bundling, but held 1.7 GB idle and got an agent OOM-killed | Memory is a real cost on a shared host | Bundle once per input state (section 8) |
| Week 4 | Deep property tests on every PR | Shipped then moved | Finished last while repeating fixed seeds PR runs already covered | Depth belongs in the sweep | Sweep runs with fresh seeds (section 5) |
| Week 4 | Caching only tiny packages on one shard | Measured and rejected | Five CI trials saved zero billed minutes because cached work was too small | Compare lookup/restore cost against removed work | Broader caching after independent lanes (section 6) |
| Week 4 | Cutting the rest of harness startup (no proxy, lazy wasm, code cache, shared/pooled runtime) | Measured and rejected | Remaining trimmable time while keeping per-file isolation was only a few percent of test time | Tests need the proxy, and a shared runtime breaks isolation | Making the server bundle load less at startup (a production change) |
| Week 4 | Cutting a shard's fixed costs (web build, test bundles, module cache) | Measured and rejected | Only seconds per shard; module cache keyed on lockfile and configs, so nearly every full run started cold | Check how often cache-key inputs actually change | A key that survives lockfile churn |
| Week 4 | Claim queue's fixed share, cross-run claims, time-only batches | Modelled and in CI; replaced | A slower runner overran the others' share; per-batch invocations repaid startup; time-only batches ignored per-file startup | Model both the slowest runner and per-file startup | Updated fixed share and per-file startup cost |
| Week 5 | Merging a declaration and cached-check spike wholesale | Folded into another change | Closed unmerged; project-level caching was built locally first | A closed spike isn't a rejected technique | — |
| Week 5 | Caching sub-second generation | Shipped then removed | Replay took 2–4× as long as regenerating | Cache overhead can exceed the work | Ordered direct generation writing only on change |
| Week 5 | npm tarball cache | Measured and rejected | Restoring 352 MB cost more than it saved | Always measure restore time | — |
| Week 5 | Duplicating remote cache in Actions cache | Shipped then removed | Hid whether remote reuse actually worked | Keep one cache layer so hits are attributable | Remote cache alone |
| Week 5 | Cached execution in rounds, two workers per group | Measured and replaced | Workers idled waiting for slow group members | Synchronized rounds idle workers | Independent lanes, one server file per task |
| Week 5 | One private cache path per lane | Measured and replaced | The path entered every key, preventing any cross-sweep replay | Anything in the environment can leak into a key | Shared storage with per-invocation status |
| Week 5 | Raising cache concurrency further | Rejected | Buffers exceeded the Worker's memory limit | Concurrency is memory-bound, not just CPU-bound | Shared byte budget instead of fixed buffers |
| Week 5 | Several broad local cached suites at once on a shared box | Measured and replaced | Warm single runs didn't hold up under concurrency: timeouts and resets | A shared-host limit, not an argument against broad checks | Fewer test slots and focused local selection |
| Week 5 | Four server files per cached task | Measured and rejected | Fewer launches, but longer shards and far more tail idle time | Coarse indivisible groups lose to fine-grained lanes | — |
| Week 5 | Fully async SQL test transport / deferred writes | Measured and rejected | Altered completion order and visibility, breaking clock-driven tests | Optimize transport while preserving caller semantics | Synchronous socket (section 10) |
| Undated | Cheap external sandboxes as runners | Measured and rejected | Roughly a third slower on average, and flaky | Don't trade every-PR wait time for pennies | — |
| By week 2 | Long-lived test boxes | Rejected | Idle time billed up to a 30-minute timeout | Lifecycle economics matter | — |
| — | A separate "fast" local command | Rejected on principle | — | Make the default command fast | — |
| — | A test mode in production code | Rejected on principle | — | Keep one code path; vary periods via settings | — |
| — | Making a fake slow to mimic a real rate limit | Rejected on principle | — | Prove behavior at the limit instead | — |
| — | Widening a production API to remove a test's last wait | Rejected on principle | — | The API is the product | — |

Rows folded into another change or closed before measurement are not failed optimizations—don't treat them as performance failures without evidence.

## 20. Thresholds cheat sheet

From [docs/pages/20-thresholds-cheat-sheet.md](../../../../docs/pages/20-thresholds-cheat-sheet.md). The source repo's starting values, as examples, not targets.

These are our starting values from one repository. Don't copy them blindly as targets—derive your own from your bottlenecks and comparable runs.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Slow test file | > 10 s in CI |
| Split a file | > ~90 s, by subject (ordinary shard files; container files have a 10-minute file timeout) |
| Shard target | 75 s of tests per worker, 6 workers, ≤ 16 shards |
| Shard length | ≤ ~2 min elapsed including setup (on a per-job rounding provider); p95 warning at 110 s |
| Full PR run / small run budget | 5 min / 3 min |
| Job budget | p95 + 15%, rounded up to 5 s |
| Small runner | `server_files + other/10 ≤ 6` → 2 vCPU, 2 workers |
| Work stealing | ~50% of estimated work fixed; queued batches of whole groups summing ~60 s of estimated work |
| Near-selection fan-in cutoff | 20 importers |
| Rust pass reuse window | 30 h (sweep refreshes at 20 h) |
| Flake priority bump | 3 occurrences in 7 days |
| Flake close | ≥ 7 quiet days and 50 clean executions (7 clean executions for sweep-only and job-level issues) |
| In-CI retry | 1, in-process; 0 locally and in proof repeats |
| Runner resize | Only when ≥ 3 runs agree on CPU |
| Re-estimate container test time | Off by > 20% |
| Local test slots | `max(2, floor(cores / 4))`, unless `TEST_SLOTS` is set |
| Wait hints | Files > 10 s |
| Like-for-like noise band | ~±40% on single comparisons in our CI; measure your own |
| Records collector | ≤ 1,500 API calls per night (counted as made); keep 1,000 in reserve |

## 4. Run only what a change can reach

From [docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md). Selection with Turborepo or Nx.

### Turborepo and Nx: their own affected runs first

**Applies when:** The repo uses Turborepo or Nx and does no selection today. **Skip when:** The repo uses neither.

Turborepo and Nx already ship package-level selection (`turbo run <task> --affected` and `nx affected -t <task>`). If your repo currently runs everything on every PR, turn that on before building a custom selector. Both tools diff against a base commit, so confirm CI fetches enough git history to reach it and passes the right PR base—check your installed version's docs, as flags and defaults change across releases.

- **Package-level reach.** A change selects every task in its package and in dependent packages according to the tool's graph. Declare edges the graph can't infer: root config, files read from disk across packages, and generated code. Unknown inputs should still select everything.
- **Verify it like any selector:** replay recent PRs and compare what it ran against what they needed ([below](../../../../docs/pages/04-run-only-what-a-change-can-reach.md#verify-the-selector-like-production-code)).
- **Don't downgrade a finer selector.** If the repo already selects by test file, keep it—replacing semantic selection with a package graph missed tests in 74 of 100 replayed PRs (above). Our planner in [`templates/plan/`](../../../../templates/plan/README.md) targets pnpm workspaces only, so in a Turborepo or Nx repo treat it as a later pilot rather than a first step.

## 5. Tiers: what runs where

From [docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md](../../../../docs/pages/05-tiers-what-runs-where.md). The release checklist each shipping path is mapped to, before any PR coverage moves to a sweep.

### Releasing what the sweep checked

**Applies when:** Any PR coverage is moving to a sweep, or releases and deploys should ship only what the sweep checked. **Skip when:** PRs keep all their coverage.

The release and deploy tiers above depend on seven steps. Map each to your own release process before deferring any PR coverage to a sweep. [`templates/github/README.md`](../../../../templates/github/README.md#release-integration-checklist) maps steps 2–7 to scripts; step 1 is the first step of `ci.yml`'s plan job.

Two prerequisites come first:

- **Prove one complete sweep.** Before routing any check off PRs or enabling the release gate, demonstrate one sweep that executed every deferred check, and list each check with evidence of its success. A sweep can report green on an unchanged commit after running only its plan, and the release helper matches a passing sweep by workflow, branch, title, and shipped content—neither confirms which deferred checks were wired in or ran. Your gate must therefore check the sweep's coverage policy or a verified coverage record (including when a sweep inherits an earlier run's result). [`release-checked.ts`](../../../../scripts/sweeps/release-checked.ts) uses `sweeps.requiredJobs` to list the jobs a release relies on: add each job there before taking its check off PRs. Checks against live systems (staging, external tools) need their own freshness rule.
- **Gate every shipping path.** Keep required coverage on PRs until every path that ships verifies a passing full run at the exact release commit (or a proven-equivalent input identity). Define behavior for missed, failed, or stale sweeps and for manual promotions. Bind direct deploys to a checked commit or artifact digest. A repo that deploys on every merge—or lacks a reliable release gate—must keep its coverage on PRs.

Our seven release steps (for npm packages with optional native children; adapt for other artifacts—for a Python wheel or sdist, verify build metadata, resolved inputs, and a clean-environment install and smoke test; for a container, verify the image digest):

1. **Reject unpublished snapshot dependency URLs** in ordinary PRs, sweeps, and releases, permitting them only in explicitly targeted manual experiments. Run the guard in [`scripts/sweeps/`](../../../../scripts/sweeps/) right after the plan job checks out.
2. **Run the content-equality guard before tagging or publishing:** shipped files must match what a passing sweep checked.
3. **Build every release platform fresh.**
4. **Pack once, then install each tarball with the plain package manager alone** (`npm` for us) and validate the installed artifacts.
5. **Publish optional platform packages before the parent package** that depends on them.
6. **On retry, publish only still-missing versions** from the same tarballs; never overwrite an already published version.
7. **After publishing, advance production to the sweep's checked commit** using an ancestor or fast-forward check.

## 6. Reuse work by its real inputs

From [docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md). Guide section 6's cache table, and the trust policy a shared cache needs.

### Task runners and their remote caches

**Applies when:** The repo already uses a workspace task runner or caches task results. **Skip when:** You would adopt a runner solely for its cache and haven't done section 4's selection replay yet.

We used Vite+, but most workspace task runners support remote caching, and each technique in this section maps to an equivalent setting. Start with the runner your repo already has; adopting a new runner purely for its cache requires running section 4's selection replay first.

| Technique | Vite+ (`vp run`) | Turborepo | Nx | Bazel | Gradle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tests as cached tasks** | Test groups defined as tasks in `run.tasks` (ours: [`test-tasks.ts`](../../../../scripts/shards/test-tasks.ts)); tasks cache by default | A `test` task in `turbo.json`; tasks cache unless `cache: false` | A `test` target with `"cache": true`, usually in `targetDefaults` | Test targets cache by default (`--cache_test_results=auto`) | The built-in `Test` task is cacheable; custom tasks opt in with `@CacheableTask` |
| **Keying by real inputs** | Automatic: records file reads, missing-file probes, and directory listings. Narrow with `cache.input` globs and `!` exclusions | `inputs` globs per task (`$TURBO_DEFAULT$` plus exclusions); `globalDependencies` for workspace-wide files | `inputs` and `namedInputs` (`sharedGlobals` for workspace-wide files), plus `externalDependencies` and `dependentTasksOutputFiles` | Each action's declared sources, dependencies, and tools (tools outside the workspace aren't tracked) | Annotated task inputs with `@PathSensitive(PathSensitivity.RELATIVE)` so checkouts at different paths share keys |
| **Environment in the key, run-specific values out** | `cache.env` keys a variable; `cache.untrackedEnv` passes one without keying it | `env` / `globalEnv` key a variable; `passThroughEnv` / `globalPassThroughEnv` pass one unkeyed; `envMode: "strict"` hides the rest | `{ "env": "NAME" }` and `{ "runtime": "<command>" }` inputs; unlisted variables aren't keyed | `--action_env` keys a variable; `--incompatible_strict_action_env` (on by default) fixes `PATH` so machines share hits | Values declared with `inputs.property(…)` are keyed; undeclared env reads aren't, so declare every one that affects the result. Keep absolute paths out |
| **Outputs to restore** | Automatic write tracking, or `cache.output`; `output: []` replays a pass without restoring files | `outputs` globs; logs always replay, so `outputs: []` suits a test pass | `outputs` per target | Each action's declared outputs from the content-addressed store | Declared `@OutputFile` / `@OutputDirectory` |
| **PRs read; only `main`'s CI writes** | `VP_REMOTE_CACHE=read` on PRs, `read-write` on `main`. Not yet in Vite+'s public docs; [`cache/remote/`](../../../../cache/remote/README.md) documents our setup | `--cache=local:rw,remote:r` on PRs (or `TURBO_CACHE` with the same value) | No client switch for self-hosted servers: give PRs a read-only token the server rejects writes for (the spec's 403 for a read-only token). Nx Cloud supports read-only tokens | `--remote_upload_local_results=false` on PRs | Enable `push` on the remote `HttpBuildCache` only in `main`'s CI (Gradle's `isCiServer` example pushes from any CI—narrow it to `main`) |
| **Checking replays** (sampled uncached rerun vs. replay) | `vp run --no-cache` on a sample; ours is `test-lanes.ts --verify-hits <n>` | Rerun the sample with both caches off (`--cache=local:`); compare `--dry=json` hashes | `NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE=true` reruns cached tasks; add `NX_SKIP_REMOTE_CACHE=true` so the probe neither reads nor writes the remote | `--noremote_accept_cached --cache_test_results=no` with uploads off; compare `--execution_log_compact_file` logs | `--rerun-tasks --no-build-cache`; `-Dorg.gradle.caching.debug=true` prints each key |
| **Trust and signing** | No signing in the protocol. Our Worker uses token digests, read tokens for PRs, and OIDC writes from `main` | `remoteCache.signature: true` with `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY` signs artifacts (HMAC-SHA256); bad signatures miss. Because the key is shared, a valid signature proves key possession, not which run wrote it | Self-hosted: bearer tokens, no signing. Nx Cloud offers end-to-end encryption (`NX_CLOUD_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) for privacy, not provenance | No signing. Blobs are content-addressed, but action-cache entries aren't signed; Bazel's docs suggest letting only CI write | No signing; HTTP Basic credentials. Gradle's docs recommend CI populates the cache and developers only read |

Sources, checked November 2026: Vite+ [task caching](https://viteplus.dev/guide/cache) and [run config](https://viteplus.dev/config/run); Turborepo [configuration](https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/configuration), [`run` options](https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/run), [environment variables](https://turborepo.dev/docs/reference/system-environment-variables), and [remote caching](https://turborepo.dev/docs/core-concepts/remote-caching); Nx [inputs](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/inputs), [caching](https://nx.dev/docs/concepts/how-caching-works), [environment variables](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/environment-variables), and [self-hosted caching](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/self-hosted-caching); Bazel [remote caching](https://bazel.build/remote/caching), [cache-hit debugging](https://bazel.build/remote/cache-remote), and [command-line reference](https://bazel.build/reference/command-line-reference); Gradle [build cache](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_cache.html), [cache debugging](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_cache_debugging.html), [incremental build](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/incremental_build.html), and [command line](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/command_line_interface.html).

**Self-hosting.** Turborepo servers implement its [Remote Cache API](https://turborepo.dev/docs/openapi) (community options include [one on Cloudflare Workers with R2](https://github.com/AdiRishi/turborepo-remote-cache-cloudflare)). Nx servers implement its [OpenAPI spec](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/self-hosted-caching#open-api-specification), configured via `NX_SELF_HOSTED_REMOTE_CACHE_SERVER` and `NX_SELF_HOSTED_REMOTE_CACHE_ACCESS_TOKEN`. Bazel accepts an HTTP or gRPC cache such as [bazel-remote](https://github.com/buchgr/bazel-remote) via `--remote_cache`. Gradle accepts any HTTP server handling GET/PUT, or its own build cache node.

**The trust design carries over.** The architecture in [`cache/remote/`](../../../../cache/remote/README.md) works in front of any of these servers: store only SHA-256 digests of tokens so config holds no secrets, issue read-only tokens to PRs, and accept writes *only* from `main`'s CI, identified by GitHub's OIDC token (checking repository, event, and ref), so there is no write secret to leak. A self-hosted server for any runner can make the same checks before storing an entry. Regardless of runner, authentication proves who wrote an entry, not that the work was honest (see [Trust](../../../../docs/pages/06-reuse-work-by-its-real-inputs.md#a-remote-task-cache-with-tests-as-tasks) below).

### Trust

- **Trust:**
  - **Authentication isn't provenance.** Any cache writer can upload a forged pass or build output that `main` later consumes; OIDC proves *who* wrote an entry, not that the work was honest. Before sharing results, inventory every writer and every release or deploy consumer, then document your policy: shared writes from protected `main` only (with branches in isolated namespaces), equivalent independent verification, or no remote reuse for anything that ships. Fresh sampling catches some faults but does not establish provenance. Our own setup accepted broader writers as known development debt. The reference implementation in [`cache/remote/`](../../../../cache/remote/) ships the narrow policy instead—writes from `main` pushes only; widen it only as a recorded decision. [Its README](../../../../cache/remote/README.md#trust-decide-who-may-write-what-main-replays) holds the writer list, the consumer list, and the policy choice.
  - CI reads with a secret token and writes via GitHub OIDC. Our broad-debt policy lets `main` pushes, same-repo PRs, and branch manual runs write; the narrow policy we recommend (and ship in `cache/remote/`) writes only from `main` pushes while PRs and dispatches read. Forks always run fresh.
  - Developers read and write with personal credentials.
  - Read failures degrade to misses, and upload failures never fail a passing task.

## 14. Local speed, and many agents on one machine

From [docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md](../../../../docs/pages/14-local-speed-and-many-agents-on-one-machine.md). What a local runner of selected tests must do before its green means they ran.

### The local runner contract

**Applies when:** A local runner executes a selected subset of tests (such as `test:cached` or a custom driver). **Skip when:** Local runs don't use selection.

`test:cached` combines a selector with a runner. A naive runner that simply invokes a selected file list can report green even when files failed to execute. Ours satisfies all of the following; because [`scripts/local/`](../../../../scripts/local/) ships only the selector, make sure any runner you write or use meets every point:

- **Form stable groups from the entire ordinary suite before filtering,** so group keys never depend on the selection. Keep local grouping separate from CI's.
- **Bound concurrent tasks** using the machine's file-slot cap.
- **Fall back to every ordinary test** if selection fails.
- **Validate explicit paths** and reject ambiguous substring matches.
- **Serialize callers** sharing a summary or cache directory: tag each invocation and round, and reject foreign or missing summaries.
- **Account for every selected file** as replayed, passed, failed, interrupted, or not run—and fail the run if execution is incomplete.
- **Support `--no-cache`** to disable reads and writes in both local and remote caches.
- **Optionally re-run a sample of hits uncached** to check cache soundness, and never count a replay as a fresh flake observation.

Let each repo supply its own database and codegen setup; the contract is independent of our stack.

## Selection planner

From [templates/plan/README.md](../../../../templates/plan/README.md). The selection planner's inputs and its limits.

### The rules, in order

1. **CI files** (`ci.yml`, called workflows, `.github/actions/`), with `--near`: both revisions are parsed as YAML and compared block by block. A changed job runs itself plus everything that waits on it, through `needs` or the `wait-for-jobs` action; a changed action runs its callers. The plan, the result, the top level, an unknown job or an unparseable file select everything.
2. **Root scripts** are classified by their callers: only tests → those tests; one CI step's tool → that job; production code → like an edit to that package; deciding selection or execution (`runScripts`), or named by the root manifest outside its tools → everything. Unknown scripts fail toward everything.
3. **Shared inputs and the checks themselves** → everything.
4. **Docs, agent guidance and ignore files** → no tests. They still get static checks and lint.
5. **Lockfile** → the packages whose resolved installs changed, then their consumers. Root importer, settings, overrides, patches → everything. Catalog-only workspace edits → nothing of their own.
6. **Package edits** → the package and its transitive consumers, from manifests plus names in imports, build commands and config paths. The deepest containing package owns a file. Cycles end at a fixed point.
7. **Test-only edits** (tests, `testing/` helpers no manifest exports) → only the tests that run them.
8. **Entry points** (`entryScoped`): a dependent of a shared library runs only its tests that load an entry exporting a changed module.
9. **Near**, with `--near`, for one integration-heavy package: tests the change edited, tests whose imports reach it climbing upward but **stopping at modules with more than 20 importers**, tests named for the changed modules, and **explicit coverage declarations** (`nearCovers`) for tests that read files from disk or run generated bundles.
10. **Covered-only** (`coveredOnly`), with `--near`: heavy proofs run on a PR only if it touches their covered paths, **even when it otherwise selects everything**.
11. **Own-job files** (`ownJob`: real containers, proofs), printed as `own_jobs=`: see [container-test reach](../../../../templates/plan/README.md#container-test-reach).
12. **Anything unknown** → everything.

Before shipping a rule change, replay it over historical diffs and compare the selection (guide section 4, "Verify the selector like production code").

### Left out of the reference

- Our repo's coverage tables, contract-vector and bundle-consumer rules: write yours as `nearCovers` and `coveredOnly` entries.
- The local mode (`--local`) that picks tests near the working tree for a pre-push command: build it from `changed-files.ts` and the same rules if you want one (guide section 14).
